patient.name: Luca Moretti
patient.complaint: Swollen, painful left knee and right ankle for 5 days, with sore red eyes
background: Barista in Camden; new sexual partner 5 weeks ago
Stinging on passing urine about 3 weeks ago, now settling

diagnosis.exam: Expect 'Which is the most likely diagnosis?' with a young man who has an asymmetrical lower limb arthritis 1 to 4 weeks after dysuria or diarrhoea, plus red eyes, mouth ulcers or a rash on the soles. Psoriatic arthritis, gout, RA and septic arthritis are the distractors.

points: Luca, 27: **left knee and right ankle** swollen for 5 days.
Both eyes **red and gritty** since yesterday.
Dysuria **3 weeks ago** after a new partner.
Limping; his right heel hurts on standing.

steps.lead: Luca's joints flared **3 weeks after** a urethritis: the classic **1 to 4 week** gap of reactive arthritis.

visual.title: Weeks from infection to arthritis
visual.label: Luca 3 weeks
visual.caption: Joint symptoms usually begin **1 to 4 weeks** after the GU or GI infection.

steps.lead: Luca is a **young man** with a likely **Chlamydia** urethritis: the most common trigger.

points: Left knee: warm effusion. Right ankle: swollen.
Tender **Achilles insertion** and a **sausage-shaped** second toe.

steps.lead: **Asymmetrical lower limb oligoarthritis**, **enthesitis** at the heel and **dactylitis**: Luca has the full pattern.

steps.q: Which feature completes Luca's classic triad?
steps.r: The triad is **conjunctivitis, urethritis and arthritis**: 'can't see, can't pee, can't climb a tree'.

steps.lead: Luca has the triad. Check his soles and penis for **keratoderma blenorrhagica** and **circinate balanitis**.
Luca's knee is aspirated: **cloudy, high white cells, but no organisms and no crystals**. That sterility separates it from septic arthritis.

steps.title: Hot swollen knee in a young man
head: Feature
Reactive arthritis
Septic arthritis

steps.lead: Most episodes settle, but Luca may develop **chronic arthritis**, and if **HLA-B27 positive**, ankylosing spondylitis.

steps.text: Do not choose **psoriatic arthritis** just because there is dactylitis and a rash. The **preceding infection**, **conjunctivitis** and **rash on the soles** make it reactive arthritis.

investigation.exam: Expect 'Which is the most appropriate investigation?' to find the trigger (urine NAAT/STI screen or stool culture), synovial fluid questions where the culture is negative and there are no crystals, and the rule to exclude septic arthritis first.

steps.lead: Luca has a hot, swollen knee and a low-grade fever, so **septic arthritis is excluded first** by aspirating the joint.

steps.title: Luca's knee aspirate
steps.text: Inflammatory but **sterile**, with **no crystals**: not septic arthritis, not gout or pseudogout.

visual.title: Synovial white cell count
visual.label: Luca 18,000
visual.caption: A high count alone cannot rule out sepsis; the **negative Gram stain and culture** are what make it sterile.

steps.lead: There is no single confirmatory test: Luca's diagnosis is **clinical**, backed by evidence of the preceding infection.

steps.q: Which test is most likely to identify Luca's trigger?
steps.r: After urethritis, the trigger is usually **Chlamydia**: test with a **first-void urine NAAT** (STI screen). Stool culture is for a post-diarrhoeal trigger.

steps.lead: Luca's **CRP and ESR are raised** and his urine NAAT comes back **positive for Chlamydia trachomatis**.

steps.text: Match the screen to the story: **dysuria or new partner → urine NAAT/STI screen**; **diarrhoea or food poisoning → stool culture** (Campylobacter, Salmonella, Shigella).
Do not expect to grow the organism from the joint. In reactive arthritis the **joint is sterile**; a positive joint culture means **septic arthritis**.

management.exam: Expect 'Which is the most appropriate initial management?' (oral NSAID, with rheumatology referral), treating a persisting trigger (doxycycline for chlamydia), and the ladder to intra-articular steroid and sulfasalazine.

steps.q: Septic arthritis is excluded. What is the most appropriate initial treatment for Luca's joints?
steps.r: **Oral NSAIDs** (ibuprofen or naproxen) are the initial treatment. IV antibiotics are for septic arthritis; sulfasalazine is for chronic disease.

steps.lead: Luca is referred to **rheumatology** and starts **naproxen**.
His Chlamydia is still present, so he gets **doxycycline** (and partner notification). If his knee stays swollen, an **intra-articular steroid** injection is next.

visual.title: Luca's recovery
visual.caption: Most cases settle over weeks to months with NSAIDs and treating the trigger.

steps.lead: If Luca's arthritis became **severe or chronic**, a **DMARD such as sulfasalazine** would be used.

steps.text: Antibiotics treat a **persisting infection**, not the arthritis itself. The joint is sterile, so NSAIDs remain the treatment for the joints.
Do not inject a joint with steroid until **septic arthritis has been excluded**. Steroid into an infected joint is a disaster.

science.exam: Expect applied mechanism questions: why the joint fluid is sterile despite a high white cell count, how HLA-B27 and molecular mimicry link infection to arthritis, and why enthesitis gives heel pain and dactylitis.

steps.lead: Luca's disease is a **seronegative spondyloarthropathy**, set off by an immune response to a **distant** GU infection.

nodes: Inflammation: high white cells in the joint

steps.lead: That is why Luca's aspirate had **18,000 white cells but grew nothing**.
If Luca is **HLA-B27 positive**, **molecular mimicry** may explain why the response keeps going after the infection has cleared.

steps.q: Why does Luca have heel pain and a sausage toe?
steps.r: **Enthesitis**, inflammation where tendons insert into bone, explains Achilles tendonitis, plantar fasciitis and **dactylitis**.

steps.lead: Luca's Achilles and toe share this **enthesitis** mechanism with ankylosing spondylitis and psoriatic arthritis.
Repeated episodes of **HLA-B27-driven** inflammation could, in a subset like Luca, progress to **ankylosing spondylitis**.

mcq.q: What is the most common cause of reactive arthritis?
Which skin lesion on the soles is fairly specific to reactive arthritis?
mcq.r: **Keratoderma blenorrhagica**: waxy yellow/brown lesions on the soles.

mcq.q: Which joint pattern is typical of reactive arthritis?
o: Symmetrical small joints of the hands

mcq.q: What are the synovial fluid findings in reactive arthritis?

Which HLA type is most strongly linked to reactive arthritis?

glossary.Reactive arthritis: Sterile inflammatory arthritis starting 1 to 4 weeks after a GU or GI infection.
glossary.Reiter's syndrome: Older name for reactive arthritis with conjunctivitis and urethritis.
glossary.HLA-B27: Class I HLA gene variant linked to reactive arthritis and other spondyloarthropathies.
glossary.Seronegative: Rheumatoid factor negative; describes the spondyloarthropathies.
glossary.Spondyloarthropathy: Family of HLA-B27 linked arthritides: AS, reactive, psoriatic and enteropathic arthritis.
glossary.Oligoarthritis: Arthritis affecting two to four joints.
glossary.Migratory: Moving from one joint to another over time.
glossary.Urethritis: Inflammation of the urethra causing dysuria and discharge.
glossary.Dysuria: Pain or stinging on passing urine.
glossary.Sterile pyuria: White cells in the urine with no growth on standard culture; think chlamydia.
glossary.Conjunctivitis: Inflammation of the conjunctiva causing red, gritty eyes.
glossary.Enthesitis: Inflammation where tendons or ligaments insert into bone.
glossary.Enthesis: The site where a tendon or ligament attaches to bone.
glossary.Dactylitis: Swelling of a whole finger or toe, giving a 'sausage digit'.
glossary.Achilles tendonitis: Inflammation of the Achilles tendon, causing heel pain.
glossary.Plantar fasciitis: Inflammation at the heel insertion of the plantar fascia.
glossary.Keratoderma blenorrhagica: Waxy yellow-brown thickened lesions on the soles or palms, fairly specific to reactive arthritis.
glossary.Circinate balanitis: Painless lesions on the glans or prepuce of the penis in reactive arthritis.
glossary.Chlamydia trachomatis: Obligate intracellular sexually transmitted bacterium; the commonest trigger of reactive arthritis.
glossary.Campylobacter jejuni: Common cause of bacterial gastroenteritis that can trigger reactive arthritis.
glossary.Salmonella: Gram-negative bacterium causing food poisoning; a post-enteric trigger.
glossary.Shigella: Gram-negative bacterium causing bloody diarrhoea; a post-enteric trigger.
glossary.NAAT: Nucleic acid amplification test; detects chlamydia and gonorrhoea DNA in urine or swabs.
glossary.Gram stain: Stain that shows bacteria in fluid; negative in reactive arthritis joint fluid.
glossary.Synovial fluid: Lubricating fluid inside a joint, aspirated for cell count, Gram stain, culture and crystals.
glossary.Septic arthritis: Bacterial infection inside a joint; an emergency to exclude first.
glossary.Molecular mimicry: Immune response to a microbe cross-reacts with similar-looking self proteins.
glossary.NSAIDs: Non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs such as ibuprofen and naproxen.
glossary.Methylprednisolone: Corticosteroid that can be injected into a joint.
glossary.DMARD: Disease-modifying antirheumatic drug that suppresses chronic inflammatory arthritis.
glossary.Sulfasalazine: DMARD used for severe or chronic reactive arthritis.
glossary.ESR: Erythrocyte sedimentation rate, a non-specific inflammatory marker.
glossary.CRP: C-reactive protein, an acute-phase inflammatory marker.
glossary.Synovium: The lining membrane of a joint that produces synovial fluid.

technique.stem: A 24 year old man has a 1 week history of a painful swollen left knee and right ankle. Two weeks earlier he had pain on passing urine after unprotected sex. Both eyes are red and sticky. There are waxy yellow-brown lesions on the soles of his feet.
technique.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?

steps.x: Diagnosis of arthritis with eye and skin signs in a young man.

clues: waxy yellow-brown lesions on the soles
steps.x: Asymmetrical lower limb arthritis 2 weeks after urethritis, conjunctivitis and **keratoderma blenorrhagica**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: Triad plus keratoderma: **reactive arthritis**.

elim: Behçet's gives oral and genital ulcers with uveitis, not keratoderma.
Disseminated gonococcal infection gives pustular skin lesions, tenosynovitis and fever.
Psoriatic arthritis needs psoriasis or nail changes and no infective trigger.
Septic arthritis is usually one joint with fever; no eye or skin signs.

steps.x: **D. Reactive arthritis.** 'Can't see, can't pee, can't climb a tree.'

technique.stem: A 31 year old woman has a swollen right knee and left heel pain 2 weeks after an episode of bloody diarrhoea following a barbecue. The diarrhoea has now settled. She has no urinary symptoms and no new sexual partners. Knee aspiration shows no organisms and no crystals.
technique.q: Which is the most appropriate investigation to identify the trigger?

steps.x: Find the triggering infection.

clues: 2 weeks after an episode of bloody diarrhoea
steps.x: Post-enteric story, sepsis and crystals already excluded.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Stool culture** for Campylobacter, Salmonella or Shigella.

elim: CT is not needed for settled food poisoning.
Colonoscopy is for suspected IBD, which a single episode does not suggest.
HLA-B27 is a risk marker; it does not identify the trigger.
Urate is for gout, and there are no crystals.

steps.x: **E. Stool culture.** Diarrhoea → stool culture; dysuria → urine NAAT.

technique.stem: A 29 year old man has reactive arthritis after a chlamydial urethritis, which has been treated with doxycycline. After 6 weeks of naproxen his right knee remains swollen and painful, though his other joints have settled. A repeat knee aspirate shows no organisms and culture is negative.
technique.q: Which is the next most appropriate step in management?

steps.x: 'Next step' for one persistent joint.
Infection treated, NSAID tried, one joint left, sepsis excluded.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Intra-articular corticosteroid injection.**

elim: Biologics are not the next step for one persistent joint.
The joint is sterile; antibiotics will not help.
Sulfasalazine is for severe or chronic disease, not a single knee at 6 weeks.
Surgery is far too early and not indicated.

steps.x: **B. Intra-articular methylprednisolone.** NSAID → treat trigger → joint injection → sulfasalazine.

technique.stem: A 26 year old man who is HLA-B27 positive develops a swollen knee and conjunctivitis 3 weeks after chlamydial urethritis. Knee aspiration shows a high white cell count but culture is negative. His arthritis persists after the infection has been treated.
technique.q: Which is the most likely mechanism of his persisting arthritis?
o: Molecular mimicry between bacterial antigens and HLA-B27-presented peptides

steps.x: A mechanism question about HLA-B27 and infection.

clues: persists after the infection has been treated
steps.x: Sterile joint, immune response continuing without the organism.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Molecular mimicry** with HLA-B27-presented self-peptides.

elim: Anti-CCP antibodies belong to rheumatoid arthritis.
IgE mast cell release is type I hypersensitivity (allergy).
Glomerular immune complexes are lupus or post-strep glomerulonephritis.
No crystals: not gout.

steps.x: **D. Molecular mimicry.** Sterile joint + HLA-B27 + distant infection.

practice.stem: A 25 year old man has a 10 day history of a painful swollen right knee and left ankle. Three weeks ago he had dysuria after a new sexual partner. Both eyes are red. His temperature is 37.5°C, pulse rate 90 bpm and BP 124/76 mmHg. There is no rash or nail change.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: Asymmetrical lower limb arthritis 3 weeks after urethritis, with conjunctivitis: reactive arthritis. Septic arthritis is usually a single hot joint with high fever.

steps.x: Diagnosis of arthritis after a GU infection.

clues: Three weeks ago he had dysuria
steps.x: Triad: conjunctivitis, urethritis, arthritis; timing fits.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Reactive arthritis.**

elim: Gonococcal septic arthritis has fever, pustules and tenosynovitis during, not after, infection.
Gout is acute monoarthritis; urate normal; no conjunctivitis.
Psoriatic arthritis needs psoriasis or nail changes.
RA is symmetrical small-joint polyarthritis.

steps.x: **D. Reactive arthritis.**

practice.stem: A 30 year old woman has a swollen left knee and pain under her right heel. Two weeks ago she had diarrhoea and vomiting for 4 days after eating undercooked chicken. Her temperature is 37.3°C, pulse rate 84 bpm and BP 118/74 mmHg. Knee aspirate:
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: Arthritis and enthesitis 2 weeks after Campylobacter-type gastroenteritis with sterile, crystal-free inflammatory fluid: post-enteric reactive arthritis.

steps.x: Diagnosis of a hot knee after food poisoning.

clues: Two weeks ago she had diarrhoea and vomiting
steps.x: Enthesitis; Campylobacter trigger; sterile fluid, no crystals.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Reactive arthritis** (post-enteric).

elim: Enteropathic arthritis needs IBD, not a short self-limiting gastroenteritis.
No crystals.
Gram stain and culture are negative.
SLE gives symmetrical small-joint arthralgia with rash and multisystem features.

steps.x: **C. Reactive arthritis.** Sterile + no crystals + preceding infection.

practice.stem: A 28 year old man develops arthritis of his left knee and conjunctivitis. Four weeks earlier he had urethral discharge and dysuria after unprotected sex. A urethral smear at the time showed white cells but no organisms on Gram stain.
practice.q: Which is the most likely causative organism of his initial infection?
practice.e: Urethritis with a negative Gram stain and sterile pyuria points to Chlamydia trachomatis, the commonest cause of reactive arthritis. Gonorrhoea shows Gram-negative intracellular diplococci.

steps.x: Organism question: which bug caused the urethritis?
Non-gonococcal urethritis; plus sterile pyuria.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Chlamydia trachomatis.**

elim: Campylobacter is a post-enteric trigger; no diarrhoea.
E. coli UTI would grow on urine culture.
Gonorrhoea shows Gram-negative intracellular diplococci on the smear.
S. aureus causes septic arthritis, not urethritis.

steps.x: **B. Chlamydia trachomatis.** Negative Gram stain + sterile pyuria = chlamydia.

practice.stem: A 27 year old man has had a swollen right knee for 2 weeks after an episode of dysuria. He also has gritty red eyes. On examination of his feet there are thickened, waxy, yellow-brown pustular plaques on both soles.
practice.q: Which is the most likely finding on his feet?
practice.e: Waxy yellow-brown plaques on the soles in reactive arthritis are keratoderma blenorrhagica. Erythema nodosum is tender red nodules on the shins.

steps.x: Name the skin finding.

clues: waxy, yellow-brown pustular plaques on both soles
steps.x: Reactive arthritis triad and a sole rash.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Keratoderma blenorrhagica.**

elim: Erythema migrans is an expanding red ring after a tick bite (Lyme).
Erythema nodosum is tender red shin nodules.
Janeway lesions are painless palm/sole macules in endocarditis.
Psoriasis gives silvery plaques on extensor surfaces; no infective trigger here.

steps.x: **D. Keratoderma blenorrhagica.**

practice.stem: A 32 year old man has a hot, swollen left knee 3 weeks after a diarrhoeal illness. He is systemically well. His temperature is 37.4°C, pulse rate 82 bpm and BP 130/80 mmHg. His GP suspects reactive arthritis and the knee is aspirated.
practice.q: Which is the most likely finding on synovial fluid analysis?
o: Sterile fluid with a raised white cell count
practice.e: Reactive arthritis gives cloudy, culture-negative fluid with a high white cell count and no crystals. Organisms mean septic arthritis; crystals mean gout or pseudogout.

steps.x: Expected synovial fluid in reactive arthritis.
Post-enteric, well: inflammatory but sterile.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Sterile fluid with a high WCC, no crystals.**

elim: CPPD crystals mean pseudogout.
Diplococci mean gonococcal septic arthritis.
Gram-positive cocci in clusters mean S. aureus septic arthritis.
Negatively birefringent needles mean gout.

steps.x: **E. Sterile fluid with a raised white cell count.**

practice.stem: A 23 year old man has painful mouth ulcers, a swollen right ankle and a sausage-shaped left second toe. Three weeks ago he had bloody diarrhoea that settled without treatment. There are painless shallow lesions on the glans of his penis. His temperature is 37.2°C, pulse rate 78 bpm and BP 122/70 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most likely diagnosis?
practice.e: Post-diarrhoeal arthritis with dactylitis, mouth ulcers and circinate balanitis is reactive arthritis. Behçet's gives painful genital ulcers and recurrent oral ulcers without a dysenteric trigger.

steps.x: Diagnosis of arthritis with mucocutaneous signs.

clues: Three weeks ago he had bloody diarrhoea
painless shallow lesions on the glans
steps.x: Dactylitis, Shigella-type trigger, **circinate balanitis**.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Reactive arthritis.**

elim: Behçet's genital ulcers are painful, usually scrotal, with recurrent oral ulcers.
Gonococcal arthritis follows GU, not GI, infection, with fever and pustules.
RF negative; RA is symmetrical small-joint disease.
The diarrhoea was a single self-limiting episode, not IBD.

steps.x: **C. Reactive arthritis.** Circinate balanitis + dactylitis + post-dysentery.

practice.stem: A 26 year old man has an asymmetrical arthritis of his left knee and right ankle and red eyes. One month ago he had dysuria after a new sexual partner. Knee aspiration showed no organisms and no crystals. He is systemically well.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate investigation to identify the trigger?
practice.e: After urethritis, screen for chlamydia with a first-void urine NAAT (STI screen). HLA-B27 is a risk marker, not the trigger.

steps.x: Which test finds the infection that triggered it?

clues: dysuria after a new sexual partner
steps.x: GU trigger; sepsis already excluded.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Urine NAAT / STI screen for chlamydia.**

elim: Blood cultures look for bacteraemia; he is well.
HLA-B27 does not identify the trigger.
RF is for rheumatoid arthritis.
Knee X-ray is normal early and does not find infection.

steps.x: **B. First-void urine NAAT for chlamydia.**

practice.stem: A 29 year old man has a 2 day history of a hot, very swollen right knee. He had dysuria 3 weeks ago. He is shivering. His temperature is 38.9°C, pulse rate 118 bpm and BP 104/66 mmHg. He cannot bear weight.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate initial investigation?
o: Synovial fluid aspiration, Gram stain and culture
practice.e: With fever, rigors and tachycardia, septic arthritis must be excluded first by joint aspiration before attributing the knee to reactive arthritis.

steps.x: Initial investigation in a febrile hot joint.
Systemically unwell: a septic joint until proven otherwise.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Aspirate the joint** for Gram stain and culture before antibiotics.

elim: HLA-B27 does not change the immediate plan.
X-ray is normal early and cannot exclude infection.
Urate is unreliable in acute gout and does not exclude sepsis.
Finding chlamydia does not exclude a septic joint.

steps.x: **D. Synovial fluid aspiration, Gram stain and culture.** Exclude septic arthritis first.

practice.stem: A 24 year old man has a swollen left knee and right ankle 3 weeks after a diarrhoeal illness. Knee aspiration shows no organisms and no crystals, and the diarrhoea has resolved. His temperature is 37.3°C, pulse rate 80 bpm and BP 122/78 mmHg. He has no history of peptic ulcer or asthma.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate initial management?
practice.e: Initial management of reactive arthritis is an oral NSAID with rheumatology referral. Joint injection is for persistent symptoms and sulfasalazine for chronic disease.

steps.x: Initial management, sepsis excluded.

clues: no history of peptic ulcer or asthma
steps.x: Post-enteric reactive arthritis, no NSAID contraindication, infection gone.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Oral NSAID.**

elim: Joint injection is for persistent symptoms after NSAIDs.
IV antibiotics treat septic arthritis; the joint is sterile.
Oral steroids are not first-line.
Sulfasalazine is for severe or chronic disease.

steps.x: **A. Ibuprofen.** Plus rheumatology referral.

practice.stem: A 27 year old man with reactive arthritis of his knee and ankle started naproxen a week ago. His joints are improving. His first-void urine NAAT has come back positive for Chlamydia trachomatis. He has no drug allergies.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate additional management?
practice.e: A persisting chlamydial infection should be treated with doxycycline, with partner notification. Ceftriaxone treats gonorrhoea.

steps.x: Additional management: treat the trigger.
Infection still present.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **Doxycycline.**

elim: Ceftriaxone is for gonorrhoea.
Ciprofloxacin is not first-line for chlamydia.
Flucloxacillin covers S. aureus, not chlamydia.
Metronidazole treats anaerobes, trichomonas and BV.

steps.x: **C. Doxycycline.** Then contact tracing.

practice.stem: A 34 year old man has had reactive arthritis for 8 months. Despite NSAIDs, treatment of his chlamydial infection and two knee steroid injections, he still has swelling of both knees and an ankle. His pulse rate is 76 bpm and BP 128/80 mmHg.
practice.q: Which is the most appropriate next step in management?
practice.e: Severe or chronic reactive arthritis despite NSAIDs and injections is treated with a DMARD such as sulfasalazine. Infection has cleared, so further antibiotics are pointless.

steps.x: 'Next step' in chronic disease.
Chronic, refractory; infection cleared.

steps.t: Make your own answer before looking
steps.x: **DMARD: sulfasalazine.**

elim: Biologics are not the next step before a conventional DMARD.
Hydroxychloroquine is used in RA and lupus, not reactive arthritis.
The infection has cleared.
Long-term oral steroids are not the answer for chronic arthritis.

steps.x: **E. Sulfasalazine.**
